window_check._: ⭐ THE WINDOW CHECK — owner ruling 2026-09-12, out of the AGEN firing-count divergence. A capture records the depth it was read at and that depth is asserted against the script's largest declared window BEFORE the numbers are used. Below the window the capture is WINDOW_TRUNCATED, not void, and only its short columns drop out of comparison. ⛔ Every field here except `bars_loaded` is RE-DERIVED by `tests/test_vendor_capture_window.py` from `tools/lookback_agreement.json` and compared against what is written — the capture cannot certify its own arithmetic. `bars_loaded` is the one observation only the rig can supply.
window_check._largest_is_2751_not_2500: ⚠️ 2,751 AND NOT THE 2,500 THE INPUT DECLARES. `maxLookback` is a tree SUM: the 2,500 `lookbackBarsHVE` input is the largest single term in `HVE Trigger`'s reach and not the whole of it. Both readers measure 2,751 and this is their number, not a transcription — and it is the conservative one, since a capture clearing 2,751 clears 2,500 too.
window_check._why_unmeasured: ⚰️ THIS CAPTURE PREDATES THE RULING BY HOURS. The rig depth was never probed, and it cannot be recovered from the artifact — only from the chart, on another visit. Named in `tests/test_vendor_capture_window.py::PREDATES_THE_MEASUREMENT`, which is a CLOSED list: a capture taken after 2026-09-12 that lands at UNMEASURED fails that rail by name.
window_check._what_the_capture_still_suggests: ⚠️ AN OBSERVATION, DELIBERATELY NOT PROMOTED TO A MEASUREMENT. `Avg Vol Line` reads 43,318,979 on the last bar and a 50-bar `sma` is `na` until it has 50 bars, so the three 50-bar columns demonstrably had their window. That is an argument, and the rule takes a reading — so they stay excluded until `bars_loaded` is read off the rig. ⛔ The exclusion is what makes not measuring cost something; reasoning around it here is how the rule would stop being one.
window_check._depth_evidence_2026_09_13: ⛔⛔ AND IT IS PROBABLY NOT JUST UNRECORDED — IT IS PROBABLY SHORT. A fresh load of this very layout on SPY 1D gives **640 bars** (2024-02-23 → 2026-09-11), measured 2026-09-13. The AGEN capture had to FORCE 4,066 bars with `Go to → 2012-01-03` to clear the 2,751 window, and the SPY capture records no such forcing. So the honest reading is that this capture was taken shallow and its `HVE Trigger` flat 0 may be an artefact of the load rather than the script's answer. ⭐ THAT IS WHY UNMEASURED IS NOT FLIPPED BY A PROBE: reading the depth TODAY measures today's chart, not the capture's, and the fix is a RE-CAPTURE at forced depth.

volume_granularity._: ⭐⭐ R-L (owner ruling, 2026-09-12): an INTEGER series compares EXACTLY after the coarser side's granularity is applied; anything the unit does not explain is a real divergence. ⛔ NOT A TOLERANCE — `seriesCompare` snaps BOTH sides to the unit and then demands equality, so a bar off by 101 shares still fails at unit 100. ⛔ AND IT IS DECLARED HERE, NEVER SNIFFED: 'every bar in this capture happens to be a multiple of 100' is not the same claim as 'this store rounds to 100'.
volume_granularity._whose: ⚠️ THE ROUNDING IS ON OUR SIDE. The ruling named the field `vendor_volume_granularity`; the vendor's own granularity is 1 — its values are multiples of nothing — and OUR store is the one quantising. Both are recorded so the field the ruling named exists and is true, and so the day a provider swaps the direction, the change is visible rather than absorbed.
